provenance.note: `Contacts` takes a whole `SignifyClient`, so the real client is driven with `globalThis.fetch` replaced by a recorder that signs its answers as a KERIA agent would. The clock and the agent's key are pinned. `PUBLIC TEST MATERIAL`: the passcode is the pinned tests' own and has never protected anything.

pinned_confirmations.note: the pinned `Contacts` case is unusually complete for this port: it asserts all five paths, all five HTTP methods, both write bodies field for field, and that a delete carries no body at all. Every one of those is recomputed here from the reference's own driven output. Outside that case the family is used three times in the whole tree, all of them `list` — twice with no arguments and once through the integration helper with a filter whose value is a regular expression.

an_unfiltered_listing_addresses_a_bare_q.note: `path` is `'/contacts' + '?' + params.toString()`, concatenated unconditionally, so a listing with no arguments addresses `/contacts?`
an_unfiltered_listing_addresses_a_bare_q.rust_decision: this port sends `/contacts`, on ADR `0028`'s three grounds applied again: Roadmap 3.10 strips the query before signing so the **signed path is identical**, an empty query is not a distinguishable resource, and Roadmap 5.3's builder cannot spell a bare `?` without a knob whose only users would be this call and `Operations.list`. Roadmap 9.2 owes it a live confirmation, as it does 6.5's.

half_a_filter_is_silently_dropped.guard: if (filterField !== undefined && filterValue !== undefined) { params.append('filter_field', filterField); params.append('filter_value', filterValue); }
half_a_filter_is_silently_dropped.note: the guard is `filterField !== undefined && filterValue !== undefined`, so naming one half without the other drops **both** — the caller asks for a filtered listing and is answered with an unfiltered one, which is the worst kind of wrong because it succeeds
half_a_filter_is_silently_dropped.rust_decision: **unrepresentable**: the two are one `ContactFilter` value, so there is no way to name a field without a value. The group stays independent, because it genuinely is.

the_prefix_is_not_encoded.note: all four single-contact paths are `'/contacts/' + pre`, so a value carrying `/` or `?` addresses a different resource — and Roadmap 3.10 signs `@path`, so it changes what the signature commits to. Roadmap 5.3's own fixture already recorded `contacts().delete('a/b')` reaching two segments.
the_prefix_is_not_encoded.rust_decision: refused twice over: the argument is Roadmap 3.4's validated `IdentifierPrefix` rather than a string, and Roadmap 5.3's builder would encode it exactly once regardless. A qualified prefix's alphabet is URL-safe Base64, so every real contact identifier reaches the path byte-identical.

the_filter_value_is_encoded.note: the query is built with `URLSearchParams` rather than by interpolation, so a filter value holding `&` **is** encoded — one of the few dynamic values the reference encodes anywhere, and the opposite of what Roadmap 7.1 found in `Oobis.get`
the_filter_value_is_encoded.rust_decision: reproduced exactly; Roadmap 5.3's builder encodes every query value exactly once

a_delete_carries_no_body.note: `delete` passes `undefined` where the writes pass `info`, and the pinned test asserts the request's body is `undefined` rather than an empty object
a_delete_carries_no_body.rust_decision: reproduced: no body is set on the request at all, which is what Roadmap 6.11's delete already does

the_info_is_an_open_bag.note: `ContactInfo` is `{[key: string]: unknown}` handed straight to `JSON.stringify`, so the body's field order is the caller's object literal's and any shape at all is accepted
the_info_is_an_open_bag.rust_decision: an **ordered document** — Roadmap 3.2's `Sad`, which is what Roadmap 6.6 settled a request body is here, so a caller controls the bytes exactly. The one narrowing is ADR `0008`'s number space: an exact integer is representable and a float is not, which is recorded as a limitation rather than worked around.

the_answers_are_cast_rather_than_decoded.note: all four reading methods return `res.json()` cast to `Contact` or `Contact[]`, so an answer of any shape reaches the caller as a contact
the_answers_are_cast_rather_than_decoded.rust_decision: decoded: both recorded wrong-shaped answers are proven refused, which is the rule Roadmap 6.8, 6.10, and 7.1 applied to their own answers. `id` is the one field the schema requires, and every other field the agent sends survives a round trip through Roadmap 4.1's open map.

a_listing_has_no_paging.note: no range, no limit, no cursor: an agent holding many contacts answers with all of them in one body, where Roadmap 6.6's identifier listing at least accepts a `Range` header
a_listing_has_no_paging.rust_decision: reproduced; the response is bounded only by Roadmap 5.1's transport limit, recorded as a limitation rather than a filter this port invents
